001.title: Tesla Died Alone. The Room Smelled Like Lightning.
001.description:
Nikola Tesla died in Room 3327 of the Hotel New Yorker on January 7, 1943. This historical docufiction episode follows the last room backward through Smiljan, childhood visions, the white pigeon, and the question of what the archive can and cannot prove.

January 7th, 1943. Room 3327, Hotel New Yorker. A maid named Alice Monaghan unlocked the door after three days of silence. The body was cold. The sheets were pulled military-precise. And the air smelled like the sky after a lightning strike - in a sealed room, in January, on the thirty-third floor.

This is the story of Nikola Tesla's life told backward from the room where it ended - through the geometric visions that replaced his sight as a child, the sparks he pulled from a cat's back at age three, the lightning storm in Smiljan, the pigeons, and the government office that arrived after death.

The question is not only how Tesla died. The question is what the archive could not hold.

002.title: The Fake City Was Real. Tesla Powered It. No One Tore It Down.
002.description:
In 1893, Nikola Tesla and Westinghouse lit the White City at the World's Columbian Exposition in Chicago. This historical docufiction episode follows Jackson Park, the Manufactures Building, staff construction, buried foundations, and the strange case of a temporary city that may not have behaved like one.

In 1893, the greatest buildings ever constructed in America were supposed to be temporary - plaster and wire over wooden frames, built to be demolished after six months. Nikola Tesla's polyphase AC system lit all of them. Then, inside the story, a demolition laborer named James Coburn puts his hands on the walls of the Manufactures Building and finds stone where plaster should have been.

Three archive fragments in the episode - a personal letter, a contractor incident report, and a 1904 soil boring survey - each point toward the same anomaly. None of them know about the others.

In the world of the episode, whatever Coburn's hands found is still below grade at Jackson Park. Below the Museum of Science and Industry. Unexcavated. Still unresolved.

003.title: Tesla Found the Frequency. CERN Found the God Particle.
003.description:
Nikola Tesla, CERN's Large Hadron Collider, the Higgs boson, the Berenstain Bears Mandela Effect, Schumann resonance, and Wardenclyffe Tower meet in this historical docufiction episode about the moment the baseline moved.

Close your eyes. Write the name.

Millions of people remember the Berenstain Bears as Berenstein. Cognitive science explains why the spelling changes in memory. It does not explain when the reports began to cluster.

In 1899, Nikola Tesla struck the Earth like a bell at Colorado Springs and found a frequency near eight hertz. In 2008, CERN's Large Hadron Collider circulated its first beam. In 2012, CERN announced the Higgs boson - the particle popularly called the God Particle. The date was July 4.

This is the story of a CERN calibration engineer, a background resonance reading, a Tromso station log, Wardenclyffe's demolition, and the question no instrument was built to answer: if the baseline moves, what happens to memories laid down before it moved?
